speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; could you tell me if you have noticed any vomiting, and if so, is it projectile or does it contain bile?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds very painful for him. Are the stools green and tarry (melena), or has he passed any blood? Also, do you notice a "sausage-shaped" mass in his abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Intussusception and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical presentation of an 8-month-old with abdominal distension, pain, and a likely "sausage-shaped" mass is classic for this condition. Please proceed with an Ultrasound of the abdomen to confirm the diagnosis and plan for reduction.
